tool_schemas.name: list_tasks
tool_schemas.description: Returns a paginated list of scheduled tasks, optionally filtered by task_type, enabled, and lifecycle status, and sorted by sort_by/sort_order; the response includes up to limit items and a cursor to request the next page (omit cursor to start from the first page). Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if any filter/sort value is not one of the supported enums or if limit is outside 1–200. Raises UNAUTHORIZED if the caller is not allowed to read tasks.

enabled.description: Filter tasks by whether they are enabled.

limit.description: Maximum number of tasks to return.

cursor.description: Cursor for pagination to fetch the next page of results.

sort_order.description: Sort order for the sorted field.

tool_schemas.name: get_task
tool_schemas.description: Retrieves a single task by task_id and returns its full configuration, schedule, and current lifecycle/enablement state. Raises NOT_FOUND if no task exists with the given task_id. Raises UNAUTHORIZED if the caller is not allowed to view the task.

tool_schemas.name: add_command_task
tool_schemas.description: Creates a new scheduled task of type command with the provided name, schedule, and shell command, and returns the created task record including its id and initial next-run calculation. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if required fields are missing/empty or schedule/command are invalid for a command task. Raises CONFLICT if a task with the same name already exists, and UNAUTHORIZED if the caller is not allowed to create tasks.

tool_schemas.name: add_api_task
tool_schemas.description: Creates a new scheduled task of type api that will call api_url using api_method and optional api_headers/api_body on the provided schedule, and returns the created task record including its id and initial next-run calculation. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if required fields are missing/empty, the schedule is invalid, headers are not string-to-string, or the method/url/body are not valid for an API task. Raises CONFLICT if a task with the same name already exists, and UNAUTHORIZED if the caller is not allowed to create tasks.

tool_schemas.name: add_ai_task
tool_schemas.description: Creates a new scheduled task of type ai that will run the provided prompt on the given schedule, and returns the created task record including its id and initial next-run calculation. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if required fields are missing/empty or the schedule/prompt are invalid. Raises CONFLICT if a task with the same name already exists, and UNAUTHORIZED if the caller is not allowed to create tasks.

tool_schemas.name: add_reminder_task
tool_schemas.description: Creates a new scheduled task of type reminder that will display a local popup notification (with sound) using the provided message and optional title on the given schedule, and returns the created task record including its id and initial next-run calculation. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if required fields are missing/empty or the schedule/message are invalid for a reminder task. Raises CONFLICT if a task with the same name already exists, and UNAUTHORIZED if the caller is not allowed to create tasks.

tool_schemas.name: update_task
tool_schemas.description: Updates an existing task’s fields (name, schedule, enablement, and task-type-specific configuration such as command/api_* /prompt/reminder_*) and returns the updated task record. Raises NOT_FOUND if task_id does not exist; raises VALIDATION_ERROR if the update payload is inconsistent with the task’s type (e.g., providing api_* for a non-api task), contains invalid values, or would leave required type-specific fields unset. Raises CONFLICT if renaming would collide with an existing task name, and UNAUTHORIZED if the caller is not allowed to modify the task.

tool_schemas.name: remove_task
tool_schemas.description: Removes the task identified by task_id and returns the removed task record (or a confirmation of removal). Raises NOT_FOUND if task_id does not exist. Raises UNAUTHORIZED if the caller is not allowed to delete tasks.

tool_schemas.name: enable_task
tool_schemas.description: Marks the specified task as enabled so it becomes eligible for scheduled execution, and returns the updated task record reflecting the new enabled state. Raises NOT_FOUND if task_id does not exist. Raises CONFLICT if the task is not in a state that can be enabled (e.g., deleted), and UNAUTHORIZED if the caller is not allowed to modify the task.

tool_schemas.name: disable_task
tool_schemas.description: Marks the specified task as disabled so it will not run on its schedule, and returns the updated task record reflecting the new enabled state. Raises NOT_FOUND if task_id does not exist. Raises CONFLICT if the task is not in a state that can be disabled (e.g., deleted), and UNAUTHORIZED if the caller is not allowed to modify the task.

tool_schemas.name: run_task_now
tool_schemas.description: Triggers an immediate execution of the specified task and returns the newly created execution record (including its execution id and initial status). Raises NOT_FOUND if task_id does not match an existing task, FORBIDDEN if you don’t have permission to run the task, and CONFLICT if the task is disabled or otherwise not runnable in its current state.
tool_schemas.implementation:
def run_task_now(task_id, **_extra):
    import json, os, datetime, time, uuid
    _DB = __import__("os").environ.get("MCP_DB_DIR") or ("./environment_mix/0219000" if __import__("os").path.isdir("./environment_mix/0219000") else "/app/database")
    def _load(n):
        try:
            with open(os.path.join(_DB, n), encoding="utf-8") as f:
                return json.load(f)
        except Exception:
            return []
    def _save(n, d):
        with open(os.path.join(_DB, n), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(d, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
    def _err(code, msg, **x):
        return {"error": {"code": code, "message": msg, **x}}

    t0 = time.time()
    now_dt = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)
    now = now_dt.isoformat()

    def _log(endpoint, status, task_id=None, extra=None):
        fname = "request_logs.json"
        path = os.path.join(_DB, fname)
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            return
        logs = _load(fname)
        row = {
            "id": "req_" + uuid.uuid4().hex,
            "endpoint": endpoint,
            "status": status,
            "task_id": task_id,
            "timestamp": now,
            "latency_ms": int((time.time() - t0) * 1000),
        }
        if isinstance(extra, dict):
            row.update(extra)
        logs.append(row)
        _save(fname, logs)

    if not isinstance(task_id, str) or not task_id.strip():
        _log("run_task_now", "error", task_id=str(task_id) if task_id is not None else None, extra={"error_code": "VALIDATION_ERROR"})
        return _err("VALIDATION_ERROR", "task_id must be a non-empty string")

    tasks = _load("scheduler_tasks.json")
    task = next((r for r in tasks if r.get("id") == task_id and r.get("status") != "deleted"), None)
    if not task:
        _log("run_task_now", "error", task_id=task_id, extra={"error_code": "NOT_FOUND"})
        return _err("NOT_FOUND", "Task not found")

    # Policy choice (must be consistent): reject manual run when disabled or deleted.
    if task.get("status") in ("deleted", "completed"):
        _log("run_task_now", "error", task_id=task_id, extra={"error_code": "CONFLICT"})
        return _err("CONFLICT", f"Task is not runnable in status '{task.get('status')}'")
    if not task.get("enabled", False) or task.get("status") != "active":
        _log("run_task_now", "error", task_id=task_id, extra={"error_code": "CONFLICT"})
        return _err("CONFLICT", "Task is disabled and cannot be run")

    executions = _load("task_executions.json")

    exec_id = "exec_" + uuid.uuid4().hex
    row = {
        "id": exec_id,
        "task_id": task_id,
        "trigger_type": "manual",
        "status": "queued",
        "scheduled_for": now,
        "started_at": None,
        "finished_at": None,
        "duration_ms": None,
        "exit_code": None,
        "stdout": None,
        "stderr": None,
        "http_status": None,
        "http_response_headers": None,
        "http_response_body": None,
        "ai_output": None,
        "error_message": None,
        "error_details": None,
        "created_at": now,
        "updated_at": now,
    }
    executions.append(row)

    # Update task last_run_at (execution attempt queued counts as attempt)
    task["last_run_at"] = now
    task["updated_at"] = now

    _save("task_executions.json", executions)
    _save("scheduler_tasks.json", tasks)
    _log("run_task_now", "ok", task_id=task_id, extra={"execution_id": exec_id})
    return {"execution": row}

tool_schemas.name: get_task_executions
tool_schemas.description: Returns a list of execution records for the given task, ordered from most recent to oldest, limited to the requested limit (default 10); this endpoint is not paginated beyond the limit parameter. Raises NOT_FOUND if task_id does not match an existing task and FORBIDDEN if you don’t have permission to view the task’s execution history. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if limit is not a positive integer.

tool_schemas.name: get_server_info
tool_schemas.description: Returns scheduler server/runtime metadata for all instances, or for a single instance when instance_id is provided. Raises NOT_FOUND if instance_id is provided but no such instance is known, and FORBIDDEN if you don’t have permission to view operational metadata. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if instance_id is not a valid identifier.

instance_id.description: Optional filter to return runtime info for a specific instance id.

metadata.name: Task Scheduler
metadata.description: This backend stores scheduled tasks of different kinds (shell commands, HTTP API calls, AI prompts, and local reminder notifications) along with their schedules, enablement state, and run configuration. The scheduler creates execution records when tasks run (either on schedule or via manual trigger)
